title: Spas and hot tubs, NEC Article 680 (2023): maintenance disconnect, indoor spa distances

source.publisher: City and County of Broomfield (CO), Building Division, 'Residential Swimming Pool, Spa, and Hot Tub Requirements' (May 2024, 2023 NEC); NFPA 2023-cycle Second Draft (680.44)
source.attribution: Source: NFPA 70 (NEC) 2023, 680.13 and 680.43 (government summary, City and County of Broomfield, 2024) — retrieved Oct 2026

rules.status: VERIFIED-2023 (government paraphrase; two pulls agree; canaries rejected). Verbatim 2023 wording, the metric value and the permanent-barrier exception UNVERIFIED for 2023
rules.rule_summary: Maintenance disconnecting means for spa/hot tub (and pool) equipment other than lighting: simultaneously disconnects all ungrounded conductors; readily accessible; within sight of the equipment; at least 5 ft from the inside walls.
quote_segments: For hard wired spas or hot tubs, there shall be a disconnecting means that is readily accessible and within
sight of the spa or hot tub, and located at least 5 feet from the inside walls of the spa or hot tub. This shall be
able to simultaneously disconnect all ungrounded conductors for the spa or hot tub or spa or hot tub equipment other
than lighting per NEC 680.13 and 430.102.
rules.two_pull_check: pull 1 and pull 2 identical (the bullet is printed in both the outdoor and indoor sections)

canaries.planted: disconnect at least 10 feet from the inside walls

quote_segments: and shall be located at least 5 feet (1524 mm) horizontally from the inside walls of a pool, spa, or hot tub
unless separated from the open water by a permanently installed barrier
that provides a 5-foot (1524 mm) or greater reach path.

rules.status: VERIFIED-2023 (government paraphrase; two pulls agree; canaries rejected) for the values below; (A)(2) also VERIFIED-draft from A2022 SD SR-8416 (round 3). Verbatim wording, the 680.43 exceptions and the other subdivisions UNVERIFIED
rules.rule_summary: Indoor spa/hot tub: at least one receptacle not less than 6 ft and not more than 10 ft from the inside walls; all receptacles not less than 6 ft; receptacles within 10 ft GFCI protected; luminaires over or within 5 ft: not less than 12 ft above maximum water level without GFCI, not less than 7 1/2 ft with GFCI, lower only if recessed or fully enclosed, listed for damp locations and GFCI protected; switches at least 5 ft horizontally; metal surfaces within 5 ft or within 12 ft vertically bonded with 8 AWG copper.
quote_segments: At least one receptacle shall be located not less than 6 feet measured horizontally and not more than 10
feet from the inside walls and all receptacles must be located not less than 6 feet of the spa or hot tub per NEC
680.43 (A) and 680.43 (A)(1). Receptacles located within 10 feet of the inside walls of indoor spas or hot tubs
shall be GFCI protected per NEC 680.43 (A)(2).
New light fixtures over and within 5 feet of indoor spas and hot tubs:
Shall be not less than 12 feet above the maximum water level without GFCI protection;
Shall be not less than 7-½ feet above the maximum water level with GFCI protection;
Switches shall be at least 5 feet from the inside wall of the spa or hot tub measured horizontally per NEC
Metal surfaces and metal raceways within 5 feet of the inside walls of the spa or hot tub or within 12 feet
vertically from the maximum water level shall be bonded with #8 copper per NEC 680.43 (D)(3).

rules.rule_summary: (A) Outlet(s) supplying a self-contained spa/hot tub, packaged equipment assembly, or field-assembled spa/hot tub: GFCI per 680.5(B) or SPGFCI per 680.5(C), as applicable. (B) Listed units with integral GFCI, if so marked: no additional ground-fault protection. (C) Gas-fired spa water heaters operating separately and above the low-voltage contact limit: GFCI.
